svg.title: Harmonica evaluation
svg.desc: The flow of harmonica eval. A checkpoint is loaded. The 110 development recordings are transcribed whole on the GPU, in 5 second chunks overlapping by half with the middle half of each kept, and their onset and sustain probabilities are held in memory. The onset and frame thresholds are either given on the command line or swept on the development activations in two stages: the onset threshold for OnP with the frame threshold held at 0.5, then the frame threshold for OnPOff at the chosen onset threshold, each walked from 0.85 down to 0.10, skipping thresholds whose best possible F1 cannot beat the best so far. The development set is scored at the chosen thresholds, giving Table 2's numbers. Then each test set is transcribed the same way, decoded at the thresholds, and each recording scored for OnP, OnPOff and Frm by worker processes; the mean over recordings is written to report.json and report.md after every set. Side panels show the chunking, the sweep on a grid of thresholds, the three metrics, and the worker pool.

g.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: harmonica eval: thresholds chosen on the development set, then every test set scored at them, as Section 4.1 and Appendix D describe.
Teal steps run on the GPU, purple ones in a pool of CPU workers; amber is what gets written. Counts are this repo's manifest.

Each set's activations stay in memory until it is scored:
Slakh's 1,388 stems (102 hours) take about 8 GB of float32.
The log-CQT of the whole recording (32 ms frames) is cut into
156-frame (5 s) chunks every 78 frames. Each chunk's middle 78
frames are kept and stitched: every kept frame saw 39 frames
(1.25 s) of context on either side.
Hatched: padding at the log-CQT's floor, log(1e-5), the silence a
training clip's padded tail reads. 32 chunks a batch, bf16.
xRT = audio seconds ÷ seconds spent on CQT, network and stitching;
reading and resampling the files is not counted.
Skipped unscored: a threshold whose mean 2·min(r, e) / (r + e) over
recordings, an upper bound on F1 for r reference and e decoded notes,
cannot beat the best so far. Decoding is cheap; mir_eval is not.
onset within 50 ms, pitch within 50 cents (mir_eval)
and offset within max(0.2 · reference duration, 50 ms)
both note lists drawn on a 25 ms piano roll, F1 over
(key, frame) cells: one grid for every model
Both lists empty scores 1, one empty scores 0. A set's score is
the plain mean over its recordings, so a one-minute clip counts
as much as a twenty-minute sonata.
mir_eval is single-threaded, and the sweep scores every dev
recording once a threshold. Workers are forked after inference,
so they inherit the activations instead of being sent them.
Each threshold: decode all recordings in parallel → check the
bound → score them in parallel. A step lasts as long as its
slowest recording, so long MAESTRO pieces cap the speed-up.
